problem.title_as_question: Why do pros swing around rather than low-to-high?
problem.definition: Players attempt to create topspin by lifting or swinging upward (low-to-high), which breaks the shoulder's natural rotational loading and release, leading to linear pushing or isolated forearm rolling instead of an effortless whole-arm drive.
prerequisites: Player attempting to hit topspin forehands with modern racket and string equipment

symptoms.description: Racket does not roll around down past the hand during finish; swing finishes without the elbow up racket down posture
Forearm rotates down while elbow stays down, indicating forearm-only roll without entire arm shoulder roll
Player feels like they are hitting down or hitting into the ground when first releasing the shoulder rotationally
Ball sprays off to the left or unintentionally crosscourt when attempting to hit harder

causes.statement: Brain is consciously focused on swinging upward or lifting the entire racket system for height rather than swinging around
Dragging the elbow linearly across the body rather than initiating a rotational arm press, forcing forearm-only rotation
Spacing too close to the body, which requires a linear push and inhibits shoulder external/internal rotation
Hand choked up too far on the handle rather than resting pinky on the flare of the butt cap, restricting topspin leverage
Accelerating trunk rotation all the way through to the target instead of decelerating short of the target to release the shoulder
Failing to coil with an open hip and ground force, leading player to search for velocity by using excessive trunk twist range of motion

solutions.summary: Press the racket in the direction you are facing at the start of the swing to load the shoulder rotationally rather than dragging the elbow linearly across the body.
solutions.external_goal: Press racket toward the direction you are facing at setup.

solutions.summary: Space farther to the right by getting weight over the hitting foot and lunging/leaning, pushing the ball away to clear room for shoulder rotation.
solutions.external_goal: Push contact point farther out to your right.

solutions.summary: Choke down until the butt cap is seated in the palm and the pinky sits on the butt cap flare to establish a long topspin lever.
solutions.external_goal: Keep pinky finger on the flare of the racket butt cap.

solutions.summary: Accelerate trunk rotation in a small pulse short of the target and let the trunk decelerate so the shoulder and arm release toward the target.
solutions.external_goal: Stop trunk acceleration short of the aiming target.

solutions.summary: Keep the hip open and drive pelvis forward while keeping shoulders back to create a quick rotational pulse in a small range of motion without over-spinning.
solutions.external_goal: Drive pelvis forward and shoulders back against an open hip.
